subject: Automated collection hold after August invoice — request for metering evidence
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@fastlane.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: FastLane Accounts <accounts@fastlane.ai>
Date: 2026-09-27T09:15:00+01:00
Subject: Collection hold notice — invoice 2026-08 (FastLane.ai)

Hi Mina,

We just received an automated dunning/collection hold notice for invoice 2026-08 (account FastLane.ai). We've reviewed our internal telemetry and believe there is a metering mismatch: your invoice shows a ~2.2M token overage vs. our reporting for the month of August.

Can you please pause any collection actions while we investigate? We need the following from Redwood to reconcile:
- Per-day token export for our account for 2026-08 (prefer CSV)
- Any metadata you use to attribute tokens (api_key, request_id, route)
- Clarify how replayed ingest vs. live requests are counted (we suspect a bulk replay for testing added tokens)
- Confirmation of VAT handling for EU entity (we expect reverse-charge)

I've attached a screenshot of the dunning email and we can provide our ingest manifest if helpful. This is blocking our accounts-payable hold until we align.

Appreciate quick confirmation.

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Ops | FastLane.ai
[jordan.ellis@fastlane.ai]
[Attachment: screenshot-dunning.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T10:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Collection hold notice — invoice 2026-08 (FastLane.ai)

Jordan,

Thanks for flagging this — sorry for the inconvenience. We're placing a temporary collection hold on our side for FastLane.ai while we investigate; collections team (cc'd) will own the timeline.

Vanessa/Ben — Jordan reports a ~2.2M token mismatch for Aug. Can you pull the per-day export and a short explainer of attribution logic (how replays are classified) and share what level of evidence we need from FastLane to grant a credit or adjustment?

Jordan: If you can send the ingest manifest and any request_id samples (preferably a couple of timestamps across the reported spike), paste them into this thread and we'll correlate. We'll aim to turn around an initial export within 48 hours.

I'll keep you posted.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T08:30:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Collection hold notice — invoice 2026-08 (FastLane.ai)

Jordan / Mina,

I've attached an initial metering export for FastLane.ai for 2026-08 and a short summary.

Summary (aggregate):
- Redwood-reported total tokens (2026-08): 18,742,190 tokens
- FastLane.provided total (per your note / our prior conversations): ~16,520,300 tokens
- Delta: 2,221,890 tokens (~13.4% of total for the month)

Preliminary observations:
- ~1.6M of the delta clusters to 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-15 between 02:00–05:00 UTC where we show a burst of replayed ingest requests on the API key associated with your environment (api_key ending in -fLx). These requests carry identical request_id prefixes and identical payload hashes which is consistent with automated replay jobs.
- The remaining ~600k tokens are spread across regular traffic windows; I see some long-response generations (seq length) on 2026-08-22 that increased per-request token counts.

What I need from FastLane to correlate and speed resolution:
1) Sample request IDs from your ingest manifest for 2026-08-14/15 (3–5 samples across the 02:00–05:00 UTC window)
2) Any CI/test-run notes that could explain automated replays around those dates

If you provide that, we will match request_id / payload-hash and then propose either a pro-rata credit or a one-time adjustment depending on whether the traffic was a test/replay.

Attachment: redwood_metering_export_2026-08.csv (compressed view: per-day token counts, attribution fields: api_key, route, request_id, timestamp, token_in, token_out)

Regarding VAT: we only show charges on the invoice net of VAT; if FastLane has an EU entity and reverse-charge applies, please send your VAT number and invoices we should re-issue (Ben to coordinate re-invoicing with accounting).

Collection hold: we'll keep the hold for up to 10 business days while we reconcile; if additional time is needed we'll extend with approval.

Ben Carter
Manager, Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood_metering_export_2026-08.csv (CSV, 212 KB)]

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@fastlane.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: FastLane Accounts <accounts@fastlane.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T13:42:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Collection hold notice — invoice 2026-08 (FastLane.ai)

Ben/Mina,

Thanks for the export — that matches the burst window we were worried about. Attached is our ingest manifest (fastlane_ingest_manifest_aug.zip) and three sample request_ids from 2026-08-14 (timestamps included). We also attached the dunning screenshot earlier.

Notes:
- The burst was an internal QA replay triggered by a staging job that mistakenly targeted a production API key. We've isolated the run and can provide CI logs showing it was a replay.
- FastLane operates under an EU registered entity (VAT: EU-123456789); reverse-charge should apply — please re-issue net invoices if possible while we sort the metering.

Requested next steps:
1) Match the three sample request_ids to the records in your export; if matched, propose a credit for the replayed token count (we expect ~1.55M tokens to be eligible)
2) Re-issue invoice 2026-08 net of VAT with the corrected usage number and updated invoice id if a credit is applied
3) Confirm collection hold remains in place until we sign off on the reconciliation

We can hop on a short call if helpful; otherwise appreciate your proposed adjustments in writing.

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Ops | FastLane.ai
[Attachment: fastlane_ingest_manifest_aug.zip (ZIP, 2.1 MB)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:00:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Collection hold notice — invoice 2026-08 (FastLane.ai)

Jordan — appreciate the quick turnaround and the ingest manifest.

Ben: please run the request_id/payload-hash correlation against the samples Jordan provided and confirm the total matched tokens and proposed credit amount. If the matches support a credit, Ben to confirm the re-issued invoice id and update the HubSpot ticket (link below).

Jordan: collection hold will remain in place until we complete correlation and issue an adjusted invoice or formal credit note. Expecting Ben to deliver a reconciliation summary by 2026-10-04 COB. If we need a call, I'll schedule after Ben posts the reconciliation.

HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/ticket/8341

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
